newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW-Polish bank BOS sees green loans rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Polish bank BOS sees green loans rise.

text.p: Polish Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS), which starts bourse trading on Monday, wants to stay focused on its core environmental lending business as the most promising fast-growth area, BOS president Jozef Koziol said on Thursday.
Koziol told Reuters in an interview BOS was set to benefit from Poland's catching up with environmental projects after decades of neglect.
He said he expected spending on environmental projects to grow from last year's estimated $1.5 billion at a rate far exceeding inflation.

"We can easily imagine annual expenditures of about $2 billion in 1997 or 1998, as needs are growing because of the European Union entry requirements... and this offers us chances to grow," Koziol said.

Koziol said environmental loans made up 75 percent of BOS's loan portfolio of 901 million zlotys in 1996. He said large industrial firms were the biggest clients while loans to local governments made up the largest part of the credit portfolio.

Koziol said BOS was also considering expanding through acquisitions or mergers as a way to defend its market position at a time when several financial institutions were working on consolidation plans.
"We would like to take over another bank, it might be an acquisition or a merger but our bank would have to maintain a leading position," he said.
"We are in talks with several banks but none have reached a stage that would allow to say anything specific," he added.
He said the bank also planned to start offering environmental insurance and therefore it would seek to raise its five percent stake in Samopomoc SA insurer possibly even to a majority stake.

"We have entered the firm with an intention to develop environment protection insurances, but the start of such a project will heavily depend on the market, we still have to do some analyses," he said.

He also said BOS was working with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), PHARE fund and the bank's main shareholder the National Environment Protection Fund on a green-equity fund, which would start with financing large environmental projects.
"The works are very advanced and I can't rule out the launch would be this year," he said.

Koziol said BOS aimed to keep its net earnings growth exceeding inflation and to retain most of the profits to make sure that the bank's capital grows at a faster rate than the banking sector average.
"According to our strategy, own funds of the bank should grow faster than average in the banking sector," he said.
BOS netted more than 50 million zlotys last year. Its balance sheet total grew last year 47 percent to 1.5 billion zlotys.
The bank's shareholder equity in 1996 amounted to 221 million zlotys.
